steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: The 4 Cs of food safety are: Cross-contamination prevention, Cleaning, Chilling, and Cooking.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cross-contamination prevention: use separate boards, wash hands after handling raw meat, store raw foods below cooked foods.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Cleaning: wash and disinfect all surfaces, equipment, and hands before and after food preparation.

steps.title: Key Fact
steps.body: Chilling: keep the fridge at 0–5°C, the freezer at −18°C or below; never put hot food directly in the fridge.

steps.title: Try it yourself
steps.body: Q: What are the 4 Cs of food safety? | Q: What is the correct fridge temperature range? | Q: Describe the correct handwashing procedure for food handlers.

steps.title: Check your answers
steps.body: Cross-contamination prevention, Cleaning, Chilling, and Cooking. | 0–5°C, which keeps food below the danger zone to slow or stop bacterial growth. | Wet hands with warm water, apply soap, rub palms, backs of hands, between fingers, thumbs, and wrists for at least 20 seconds, rinse thoroughly, and dry with a clean paper towel.

steps.title: Exam tips
steps.body: Always mention the 4 Cs when asked about food safety — this is a mark-scheme favourite. Be specific about temperatures: fridge 0–5°C, freezer −18°C, core cooking temp 75°C, danger zone 5–63°C. When asked about personal hygiene, list at least four practices: handwashing, clean apron, tied-back hair, covered cuts, no jewellery, not working when ill. For kitchen design questions, focus on how the layout prevents cross-contamination (separate areas for raw and cooked food).
